summary: Feed s126_double is degraded: IDS port overloaded by 321% microbursts (3.21 Gbps vs 1 Gbps) and 50% of traffic missing VLAN 20 tags, causing packet drops and blind spot for VLAN 20.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/TAP stripping 802.1Q tags or trunk not forwarding VLAN 20; 50% of packets arrive untagged and required VLAN 20 is never seen, while IDS requires VLANs 10 and 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to all VLAN 20 traffic and cannot apply VLAN-based policies/correlation; ~50% coverage loss for that segment, lateral movement in VLAN 20 goes undetected.

recommended_fix.why: Restore end-to-end 802.1Q preservation on TAP/broker trunk to deliver VLAN 20 tagged to IDS for correct segmentation and detection.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peak at 3.21 Gbps in 1ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port (321% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals); broker forwards aggregate without load-balancing or buffering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops packets during bursts, fails to reassemble TCP flows and match signatures; IDS needs full payload and both directions, so drops create critical detection gaps for exploits.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across multiple IDS ports or upgrade tool port to absorb 3.21 Gbps bursts without drops; slicing/filtering not viable as IDS needs full payload.
